Paused(address).details: Emitted when the pause is triggered by `account`.

RoleAdminChanged(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32.details: Emitted when `newAdminRole` is set as ``role``'s admin role, replacing `previousAdminRole` `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is the starting admin for all roles, despite {RoleAdminChanged} not being emitted signaling this. _Available since v3.1._

RoleGranted(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is granted `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call, an admin role bearer except when using {AccessControl-_setupRole}.

RoleRevoked(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is revoked `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call:   - if using `revokeRole`, it is the admin role bearer   - if using `renounceRole`, it is the role bearer (i.e. `account`)

Unpaused(address).details: Emitted when the pause is lifted by `account`.

params._dataRef: Swarm reference of the round document with the full reveal list (or its keccak256). Only emitted.
params._revealCount: Number of reveals in that list.
params._revealsHash: Merkle root of the reveals in the published order (leaves keccak256(overlay, depth, hash, nonce), built as for `_commitsHash`). bytes32(0) for an empty list, and only for an empty list.

params._commitCount: Number of commits in that list.
params._commitsHash: Merkle root of the signed commits, sorted by owner: leaves keccak256(owner, obfuscatedHash), padded with zero to a power of two, nodes keccak256(left, right). A node checks its own commit with a Merkle proof against this root and `_commitCount` (prover/crates/vm, `list_verify`).
params._dataRef: Swarm reference of the round document with the full commit list (or its keccak256 if the prover does not upload). Only emitted.

params._witness: abi.encode(ClaimWitness{proof1, proof2, proofLast}): the three arguments of Redistribution.claim as one value.

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleGranted} event.

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been revoked `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `account`. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

params._proofBytes: SP1 Groth16 proof (empty with the mock verifier).
params._publicValues: ABI-encoded PublicValues committed by the SP1 program.

anchorBlockHash(uint64).notice: Hash of block roundStart - 1. The round anchor (neighbourhood selection) is keccak256(abi.encode(prevrandao of that block, round)): prevrandao, not the block hash, because a block builder can grind a block hash but not prevrandao. Nodes read prevrandao (mixHash) from the header.

anchorEmpty(uint64).notice: Liveness fallback: if no prover anchored the round in blocks 16-19, anybody can anchor it with an empty commit list in blocks 20-23. The nodes then use forceCommit and forceReveal (still open), and any prover can settle the round from data that is all on chain. Without this, a prover that stops makes every round unsettleable, and the forced entries count for nothing.

anchorReveals(uint64,bytes32,uint32,byte.notice: Fix the set of off-chain reveals for the current round, so a node can check that its reveal is in it and call forceReveal before the reveal phase ends if not. Called once per round, after anchorRound, by a prover. A round settles without it; then only forced reveals count.

anchorRound(uint64,bytes32,uint32,bytes3.notice: Fix the set of off-chain commits for the current round, before any reveal and before the seed exists. Called once per round by a prover during the anchor phase.

applyVerifier().notice: Make the pending verifier change take effect, once its delay has passed. Anybody can call it.

commitDigest(uint64,bytes32).notice: The digest a node signs (EIP-191 personal_sign) for an off-chain commit. Binds the commit to this chain, this contract and this round, so it cannot be replayed elsewhere.

forceClaim(uint64,bytes).notice: Censorship escape hatch for the storage evidence: post the claim witness on chain. The proof for this round must consider it. Anyone holding the truth's sample can submit it; the payout always goes to the selected winner.

forceCommit(uint64,bytes32).notice: Censorship escape hatch: commit on chain. The proof for this round must include it. Open until the reveal phase, so a node has 4 blocks after the anchor phase to react to the list.

forceReveal(uint64,bytes32,uint8,bytes32.notice: Censorship escape hatch: reveal on chain. The proof for this round must consider it. Only the staked owner of `_overlay` can submit it, once per round. Open until the seed block, so a node has 4 blocks after the reveal anchor phase to react to the list.

proposeVerifier(address,bytes32).notice: Propose a new verifier or program. This is the upgrade key of the whole game: a verifier that accepts anything could pay the pot to anybody. So a change takes effect only `verifierDelay` seconds after the proposal (`applyVerifier`), and everybody can see it coming. A new proposal replaces the pending one and starts the delay again.

rounds(uint64).notice: The state of a round, or all zero if nothing happened in it (or its ring entry was reused).

seedBlockHash(uint64).notice: Hash of the seed block, available from block seedBlock(round) + 1. The selection seed is keccak256(abi.encode(round anchor, prevrandao of the seed block)).

settleRound(bytes,bytes).notice: Settle a round with a proof of the Redistribution VM. Permissionless: the proof is the authorisation. Pays the submitter `proverFeeBps` of the pot.

stakeDigest(address[]).notice: Same rule the VM uses to bind stake records into the proof. Uses the raw StakeRegistry record, not nodeEffectiveStake: that one depends on block.number (it is 0 while frozen), so a value read by the prover one block earlier could differ. The VM derives effective stake from these fields and the oracle price (stakePrice), exactly as StakeRegistry.calculateEffectiveStake does.

warmRing(uint64,uint64).notice: Fill ring entries once with non-zero values, so that the first round that uses an entry also pays only for writes to used slots. Optional: without it, each entry pays the new-slot cost once, on its first use. Leaves an entry that a round already uses as it is.

wrapCommit(bytes32,uint8,bytes32,bytes32.notice: Same as Redistribution.wrapCommit: the obfuscated commit hash.

userdoc.notice: Replaces Redistribution. The Schelling game (commit, reveal, truth and winner selection, freezes, redundancy count for the price oracle), the claim's storage evidence (chunk inclusion proofs, postage stamps, SOC signatures, reserve size estimate) and the postage accounting (batch expiry and the pot, which PostageStamp.expireLimited did on chain) run off chain in the Redistribution VM (prover/crates/vm). A prover proves the VM run with SP1 and this contract checks the proof and applies the result: pays the winner the proven pot from PostageStampZK, freezes stakes and adjusts the price. See docs/ZK-SETTLEMENT.md. Round layout, in blocks relative to the round start. ROUND_LENGTH = 64: with 12 s blocks a round is about 12.8 minutes, the same time as the Gnosis round of Redistribution (152 blocks x 5 s).   [ 0, 16)  commit         nodes send signed commits to a prover; or call forceCommit   [16, 20)  anchor         a prover calls anchorRound(commitsHash) once   [20, 24)  commit check   nodes check the anchored list; a node left out calls forceCommit   [24, 40)  reveal         nodes send reveals to a prover; or call forceReveal   [40, 44)  reveal anchor  the prover calls anchorReveals(revealsHash) once   [44, 48)  reveal check   nodes check the anchored reveals; a node left out calls forceReveal   48        seed block     its prevrandao becomes the selection seed. Nobody chooses it   [49, 64)  claim          a truth-teller sends the claim witness to a prover; or calls forceClaim   [49, ...) settle         anyone calls settleRound(publicValues, proof), rounds in increasing order.                            A round whose truth has no valid witness ("unclaimed") settles only from 64 forceCommit stays open until 24 and forceReveal until 48, so the last 4 blocks of each window come after the anchor: a prover that leaves a node out of an anchored list cannot stop it from going on chain. Without anchorReveals the prover could keep a commit and drop its reveal, and so freeze an honest node. Nothing in this contract decides who won. It only checks that the proof's public inputs match what the chain knows (anchor, seed, commit set, forced queues, stake records, game state, parameters) and then executes the proof's outputs.
